CONTAINS direction: larynx (whole) to superior-laryngeal-nerve (part).

The conus elasticus definition (parameter 4) states it is 'continuous superiorly with the cricothyroid membrane and with the vocal ligaments (which form its free upper borders).' The pulmonary-acinus definition includes alveolar-sac as its terminal constituent — the terminal clusters of alveoli. Direction: whole (pulmonary-acinus) to part (alveolar-sac). Literal parthood: the acinus comprises these sacs as one of its three structural components.

CONTAINS test: the saccule is a part within the supraglottic territory.

The alveolus is the microscopic air sac within the lung parenchyma where gas exchange occurs. The alveolus is physically contained within the lung as its terminal functional unit.

The subsegmental bronchi are fourth-level branches within the bronchial tree hierarchy, the last generation still bearing hyaline cartilage. They are literal parts of the tree's hierarchical structure (Law 10).

The accepted quadrangular membrane definition lists the hyoepiglottic ligament as its thickened superior edge — a thickening of the membrane's own fibrous substance, not a separate structure bounding it. Direction: whole (membrane) to part (ligament).

Law 10 part-whole test: the pharynx accepted definition (v1) explicitly enumerates salpingopharyngeus as one of the longitudinal muscles in parameter (2). The vocalis muscle is the deep medial portion of the thyroarytenoid. The cricothyroid muscle's accepted definition carves its innervation as 'external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.' Constitutive dependency. Direction correct.

The thyroarytenoid muscle's accepted definition carves its origin as 'anterior inner surface of the thyroid cartilage angle.' Removal test: remove the thyroid cartilage and the muscle loses its anterior anchor — it cannot operate as the muscle spanning thyroid to arytenoid. Constitutive attachment dependency. Direction correct.

The terminal bronchiole arose from the subsegmental bronchus through hierarchical branching. Developmentally and hierarchically, the subsegmental bronchus gives rise to the terminal bronchiole as the next generation (approximately generation 22–23 from the trachea), making the subsegmental bronchus the prior generation in the branching lineage.

The middle pharyngeal constrictor is the intermediate of the three constrictor muscles forming the muscular walls of the pharynx. CONTAINS test (Law 10) stated with result: the small-airway map enumerates its membership in parameter 1 ('the category is the bronchioles and their branches down to the respiratory bronchioles'), so the bronchiole is literally a part inside the small-airway category. The laryngocele's definition carves its origin as distension of the laryngeal saccule (parameter 1), and the laryngeal ventricle's accepted definition carves the saccule as the blind pouch of the ventricle's anterior portion (parameters 2 and 3). The thyrohyoid membrane is a ligament connecting the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid bone, explicitly listed in the framework definition as one of the inter-cartilaginous ligaments and membranes.

The vagus-nerve definition explicitly carves recurrent laryngeal branches as parameter 3: right hooks under subclavian, left under aortic arch, both ascending in tracheoesophageal groove. Direction: whole (vagus-nerve) to part (recurrent-laryngeal-nerve).

The cricothyroid membrane definition (parameter 2) explicitly lists 'the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve and the superior laryngeal vessels passing on its deep surface' as a component relationship. Per the vocal ligament definition: 'the free superior margin of the cricothyroid membrane.' Per the cricothyroid membrane definition: 'its free superior border thickens into the vocal ligament.' The ligament is literally the thickened superior edge of the membrane.

The cricothyroid-membrane definition carves the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve passing on its deep surface. This is not a genuine CONTAINS. I should file a proper edge or skip.

INSTANCE_OF test (Law 9a) stated with result: a competent pulmonologist or histologist would call the respiratory bronchiole a bronchiole — the respiratory bronchiole map is a specific member of the bronchiole map's human-made category of cartilage-free airway branches distal to the segmental bronchi. The cricothyroid joint is the articulation between the inferior horns of the thyroid cartilage and facets on the cricoid cartilage. The thyroepiglottic ligament connects the epiglottis to the thyroid cartilage and is listed in the larynx definition's parameter (1) as part of the cartilaginous framework: 'thyroid, cricoid, and epiglottic cartilages plus the paired arytenoid cartilages.' The cricothyroid muscle inserts on the inferior horn and lower border of the thyroid cartilage. Remove the thyroid cartilage and the muscle loses its insertion — it ceases to operate. The carina is the midline cartilaginous ridge at the inferior terminus of the tracheal lumen where it bifurcates (definition parameter 2). The carina is literally a physical part of the tracheal structure, not a separate organ.

The cricothyroid membrane's superior border is the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage. Operational DEPENDS_ON test (Law 8): remove the thyroid cartilage and the membrane loses its superior anchor — it can no longer function as the fibrous sheet between the two cartilages. The membrane's defined role requires both attachment points. Not identity and not purpose (Law 8c).

The supraglottis definition explicitly carves the laryngeal ventricles (spaces between false and true vocal folds) as parameter 1 of the structures it includes. Laryngeal-ventricle maps that space. Law 10 test: the laryngeal framework is literally a part inside the larynx — a material composite (the six cartilages with their inter-cartilaginous ligaments and membranes) physically within the organ, not a boundary of a region. The larynx contains the vocal folds as integral structures within the glottic compartment — the paired mucosal folds that vibrate to produce voiced sound.

Trachea as anatomical map serves the vagus nerve concept by providing a structural referent for vagal innervation description.

INSTANCE_OF test (Law 9a) stated with result: a competent pulmonologist or histologist would call a respiratory bronchiole 'a bronchiole' — it is a cartilage-free airway branch distal to the segmental bronchi, fitting the bronchiole carve (no hyaline cartilage plates, under 1 mm diameter, smooth muscle wall). The thyroepiglottic ligament connects the epiglottic apex and lateral margins to the thyroid cartilage angle, situated within the laryngeal framework anterior to the laryngeal inlet. Its presence is required for the epiglottis to maintain its anatomical position within the laryngeal apparatus.

Law 10 test stated with result: the laryngeal-inlet definition explicitly lists the epiglottis as a boundary structure in parameter (1) — 'anteriorly bounded by the epiglottis.' The trachea (cartilaginous tube C6 to T4-T5) terminates at the carina where it bifurcates into the bronchi. Anatomically, the bronchi arise from the inferior termination of the trachea — the carina is the transition point. The bronchi are the direct anatomical continuation of the tracheal lumen. The trachea's structural design (16-20 C-shaped rings, mucociliary escalator) is adapted to deliver air to the branching bronchial tree. The bronchi could not exist without the tracheal conduit above them.
The bronchus depends on vagal innervation for bronchial smooth muscle tone control; removing vagal input stops parasympathetic bronchoconstriction and sympathetic bronchodilation regulation.
